items.title: Sidereus Nuncius (Venice, 1610), title page - Library of Congress copy
items.depicts: Title page of the first edition, in a colour scan of a worn copy with stab-sewn spine at left. Visible text includes 'SIDEREVS NVNCIVS ... GALILEO GALILEO PATRITIO FLORENTINO ... PERSPICILLI ... QVATVOR PLANETIS Circa IOVIS Stellam ... MEDICEA SIDERA NVNCVPANDOS DECREVIT' above a woodcut printer's device, with the imprint 'VENETIIS, Apud Thomam Baglionum. M DC X.' at the bottom.
items.evidence: LoC record title: 'Sidereus nuncius : magna longeque admirabilia spectacula pandens ... quae à Galileo Galileo, patritio Florentino ... perspicilli nuper à se reperiti beneficio sunt obseruata in lunae facie ... apprime verò in quatuor planetis circa Iouis stellam disparibus interuallis, atque periodis, celeritate mirabili circumuolutis ... atque Medicea sidera nuncupandos decreuit'; imprint 'Venetijs : Apud Thomam Baglionum, MDCX [1610]'. The year 'M DC X' (1610) is printed on the page itself.
items.licence: Public domain (printed Venice 1610). Library of Congress, Rare Book & Special Collections, QB41 .G17 1610; no rights advisory on the record (LoC: 'the Library generally does not own rights in its collections').

items.title: Sidereus Nuncius (1610), p. 17: start of the Jupiter observations, 7 January 1610
items.depicts: Printed text page headed 'RECENS HABITAE. 17'. It announces 'quatuor PLANETAS' never seen from the world's beginning to our time, then 'Die itaque septima Ianuarij instantis anni millesimi sexcentesimi decimi ... cum caelestia sydera per Perspicillum spectarem, Iupiter sese obviam fecit' (on 7 January of this year 1610 ... while viewing the heavens through the telescope, Jupiter presented itself). The first diagram is at the bottom: 'Ori.  *  * O  *  Occ.' (Jupiter as a circle with three small stars in a line).
items.evidence: LoC record title: 'Sidereus nuncius : magna longeque admirabilia spectacula pandens ... quae à Galileo Galileo, patritio Florentino ... perspicilli nuper à se reperiti beneficio sunt obseruata in lunae facie ... apprime verò in quatuor planetis circa Iouis stellam disparibus interuallis, atque periodis, celeritate mirabili circumuolutis ... atque Medicea sidera nuncupandos decreuit'; imprint 'Venetijs : Apud Thomam Baglionum, MDCX [1610]'. The page text quoted in 'depicts' was read from the scan itself (LoC page image 41).
items.licence: Public domain (printed Venice 1610). Library of Congress, Rare Book & Special Collections, QB41 .G17 1610; no rights advisory on the record (LoC: 'the Library generally does not own rights in its collections').

items.title: Sidereus Nuncius (1610): page recording the first sighting of all four 'Stellulae' around Jupiter
items.depicts: Text page headed 'OBSERVAT. SIDEREAE' with three printed diagrams in the form 'Ori. ... O ... Occ.' (Jupiter as a circle with small stars beside it). The middle entry reads 'Die decimatertia primum à me quatuor conspectae fuerunt Stellulae in hac ad Iouem constitutione' (on the 13th, four little stars were seen by me for the first time, in this arrangement around Jupiter), followed by the diagram ' * O** * '. The lower diagram (the 15th) shows Jupiter with four stars, all to the west. There is a torn lower edge on this leaf.
items.evidence: LoC record title: 'Sidereus nuncius : magna longeque admirabilia spectacula pandens ... quae à Galileo Galileo, patritio Florentino ... perspicilli nuper à se reperiti beneficio sunt obseruata in lunae facie ... apprime verò in quatuor planetis circa Iouis stellam disparibus interuallis, atque periodis, celeritate mirabili circumuolutis ... atque Medicea sidera nuncupandos decreuit'; imprint 'Venetijs : Apud Thomam Baglionum, MDCX [1610]'. (i.e. the record itself names 'quatuor planetis circa Iouis stellam'). The 'decimatertia ... quatuor' wording is on the page (LoC page image 44).
items.licence: Public domain (printed Venice 1610). Library of Congress, Rare Book & Special Collections, QB41 .G17 1610; no rights advisory on the record (LoC: 'the Library generally does not own rights in its collections').

items.title: Sidereus Nuncius (1610), p. 23: successive diagrams of Jupiter's moons ('Medicean stars')
items.depicts: Text page headed 'RECENS HABITAE. 23' with five 'Ori. ... O ... Occ.' diagrams down the page. The small stars change position and number from entry to entry around the circle that stands for Jupiter (e.g. '* O *   *', '* *O * *', '** O * *', '* O *'). It includes 'Die quarta hora secunda circa Iouem quatuor spectabant Stellae, orientales duae, ac duae occidentales'.
items.evidence: LoC record title: 'Sidereus nuncius : magna longeque admirabilia spectacula pandens ... quae à Galileo Galileo, patritio Florentino ... perspicilli nuper à se reperiti beneficio sunt obseruata in lunae facie ... apprime verò in quatuor planetis circa Iouis stellam disparibus interuallis, atque periodis, celeritate mirabili circumuolutis ... atque Medicea sidera nuncupandos decreuit'; imprint 'Venetijs : Apud Thomam Baglionum, MDCX [1610]'. The record's 'circumuolutis' ('revolved around' Jupiter) supports the orbiting claim; the diagrams are on the page (LoC page image 53).
items.licence: Public domain (printed Venice 1610). Library of Congress, Rare Book & Special Collections, QB41 .G17 1610; no rights advisory on the record (LoC: 'the Library generally does not own rights in its collections').

items.title: Sidereus Nuncius (1610): two etched views of the Moon from Galileo's telescope drawings
items.depicts: A page with two stacked square plates, each a round lunar disc half-lit, with a ragged terminator, mottled maria, and in the lower disc a large round crater on the shadow line. The page is otherwise blank, with the faint offset of a running head at the top.
items.evidence: LoC record note: 'Contains both woodcut and engraved illustrations; moon illustrations from Galileo's own drawings.' Record title: '... obseruata in lunae facie ...' (observed on the face of the Moon).
items.licence: Public domain (printed Venice 1610). Library of Congress, Rare Book & Special Collections, QB41 .G17 1610; no rights advisory on the record (LoC: 'the Library generally does not own rights in its collections').

items.title: Galileo Galilei. Line engraving by O. Leoni, 1624
items.depicts: An oval bust portrait of Galileo, bearded, with a flat white collar and a buttoned doublet, looking toward the viewer. Inside the plate: 'Galileus Galileus Florentinus', 'Superior licentia 1624', 'Eques Octauius Leonus Romanus pictor fecit'. The print is on an old brownish mount with a pasted handwritten label: 'Ritratto di Galileo inciso nel 1624, cioè diciotto anni avanti la sua morte, dal cav.re Ottavio Leoni pittore Romano. Rarissimo', and 'B.27' in ink.
items.evidence: Wellcome record ndyr24yj: 'Galileo Galilei. Line engraving by O. Leoni, 1624, after himself [?].' Contributor 'Leoni, Ottavio Mario, 1578-1630'; production date 1624; '1 print : engraving'; Wellcome Collection 3359i.
items.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome Collection; IIIF image V0002118ER)

items.title: Scenographia Systematis Mundani Ptolemaici - Andreas Cellarius, Harmonia Macrocosmica (Amsterdam: Valk & Schenk, 1708), plate 2
items.date: 1708 printing (Amsterdam, Valk & Schenk) of Cellarius' plate first published 1660/61
items.depicts: A hand-coloured double-page engraved plate. A large terrestrial globe (Europe, Africa, Asia, India) sits at the centre of an armillary sphere, with orbits labelled LVNA, MERCVRIVS, VENVS, SOL, MARS, IVPITER and SATVRNVS circling the Earth and a zodiac band carrying sign figures. Allegorical figures and putti hold title cartouches reading 'SCENOGRAPHIA SYSTEMATIS MVNDANI PTOLEMAICI' with 'Prostant Amstelaedami apud Gerardum Valk et Petrum Schenk'. Scholars with globes and an observer with a cross-staff appear in the lower corners.
items.evidence: LoC record 2011589506: 'Harmonia macrocosmica, seu, Atlas universalis et novus ...', 'Amstelodami : Apud Gerardum Valk & Petrum Schenk, 1708.', 'Cellarius, Andreas'; '1 atlas ... 29 [i.e. 34] double leaves of plates) : hand col. maps'. The plate title 'Scenographia Systematis Mundani Ptolemaici' is engraved on the plate (image 4 of 36, numbered 2).
items.licence: Public domain (published 1708). Library of Congress Geography and Map Division, G1000.2 .C4 1708; no rights advisory on record.

items.title: Galileo offering his telescope to three women (possibly Urania and attendants) - engraved frontispiece, Opere di Galileo Galilei, 1655-56
items.date: [1655] (frontispiece of Opere di Galileo Galilei, Bologna 1655-56, v.1 1656)
items.depicts: A black-and-white copy-negative scan of an engraving, with a black film border and a handwritten number at the bottom. An elderly bearded Galileo in a long robe kneels at left, raising one hand toward the sky and holding out a long tube telescope that three seated female figures take hold of. Above is a radiant sun-like body with small bodies around it. Columns and drapery are at right, and ships and a cannon are in the left background.
items.evidence: LoC record 2006690469: '[Galileo offering his telescope to three women (possibly Urania and attendants) seated on a throne; he is pointing toward the sky where some of his astronomical discoveries are depicted]', date '[1655]', '1 print : engraving', 'Illus. in: Opere di Galileo Galilei .... Bologna : Per gli hh del Dozza, 1655-56 [v.1, 1656]'.
items.licence: No known restrictions on publication in the U.S. (LoC rights advisory); engraving of 1655-56, public domain. Reproduction LC-USZ62-110447.

items.title: Galileo demonstrates his findings to the Doge, 1609 - engraving by J. P. Le Bas, 1739 (LATER ILLUSTRATION)
items.depicts: An 18th-century engraved book frontispiece of a crowded night scene under a star-filled sky, lit by raised torches. A robed man at left points to a circular diagram held up before a seated dignitary in a ducal cap, surrounded by onlookers. An armillary sphere is at left, and two youths sit drawing on the floor in the foreground. Lettering: 'Frontispice IVe Tome', 'Dessiné et Gravé par J.P. Le Bas', 'LA LUNETTE DE HOLLANDE apliquée à l'Astronomie, en 1609'. The telescope itself is not prominent at this scale.
items.evidence: Wellcome record rfcvbyc9: 'Astronomy: Galileo, after using the telescope on the bell-tower of St Mark's Square, Venice, demonstrates his findings to the Doge, 1609. Engraving by J. P. Le Bas after himself, 1739.' Description: 'Galileo Galilei demonstrated the telescope to the Doge Leonardo Donà on the Campanile di San Marco on 21 August 1609'. Production '[Paris] : [Veuve Estienne], [1739]'.
items.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome Collection; IIIF image V0024830)

items.title: Galileo with his telescope in the Piazza San Marco, Venice - wood engraving (LATER ILLUSTRATION, undated)
items.date: undated (catalogue gives no date; later depiction, not a period image)
items.depicts: A wood engraving of a night scene before the Doge's Palace arcades in Piazza San Marco, with the two columns and gondolas on the lagoon at right and stars overhead. A long telescope on a stand is angled up at the sky, surrounded by a crowd of robed senators in caps, one leaning in to look. Below the image is a handwritten pencil annotation: 'Galilée montre au sénat de Venise les satellites de Jupiter'.
items.evidence: Wellcome record ddkpgknd: 'Astronomy: Galileo with his telescope in the Piazza San Marco, Venice. Wood engraving.' '1 print : wood engraving'; Wellcome Collection 46322i. The Jupiter-satellites wording is only a pencil note on the sheet, not part of the catalogue record.
items.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome Collection; IIIF image V0024831)
